name: hra-3d
title: HRA-3D — Model Coverage on the Human Reference Atlas 3D Anatomy
lead:
This investigation follows hra-integration and builds the 3D-anatomy side
of the fetch-and-compare spine: the full ASCT+B-3D crosswalk + a
glomerulus FTU digital object (Task A), organ-granularity model coverage
crossed with the biomodel-DO index (Task B), model->AS->GLB-node spatial
linkage (Task C), and a materialized, self-contained three.js GLB viewer
pack that renders coverage/links on a kidney reference-organ 3D model
(Task D). This realizes the DynXR proposal's Aim 2 T2.1 (HRA 3D dataset
access) and T2.2/T2.4 (spatially-grounded, transparent model-coverage
visualization); see references/sources/dynxr-proposal.md and
references/sources/hra-wpp-context.md. A later full-corpus pass
(`corpus-coverage`) retrieves and organ-tags all 1,096 curated BioModels
(82 organ-tagged) and re-crosses them against the same crosswalk, showing
the query-scoped `model-coverage-3d` study substantially undercounts real
coverage — including missing kidney entirely.
question:
Which of the HRA's 1,730 Uberon-keyed anatomical structures (2,295 raw
ASCT+B-3D crosswalk rows, 114 source-organ GLBs) are covered by a
mechanistic model — at a single query's scale and at the full
1,096-model curated-corpus scale — and can we view that coverage/linkage
directly on the 3D anatomy?
hypothesis:
The full ASCT+B-3D anatomical-structure crosswalk (2,295 rows, 1,730 with
a resolvable Uberon CURIE, below the ~81 per-organ reference-organ GLBs)
and a sub-organ-scale FTU digital object (glomerulus) are both loadable
via thin Steps; crossing the crosswalk with the hra-integration
investigation's biomodel-DO organ->models index (at organ granularity) is
enough to mark model coverage over anatomical structures/organs and to
join each covered model to the exact GLB scene node it maps to — giving a
coverage/linkage layer that a three.js viewer can render directly on a
reference-organ 3D model, without a heavyweight per-AS-node
model-matching pipeline. Confirmed: a single 25-result query covers only
58/1,730 AS nodes (liver + pancreas), while crossing the full curated
1,096-model corpus covers 635/1,730 (31/114 organs) — an order of
magnitude wider, and wide enough to newly reach kidney.

executive.what_is_this:
Builds the 3D-anatomy side of the fetch-and-compare spine: the full
ASCT+B-3D crosswalk and a glomerulus FTU digital object, organ-
granularity model coverage crossed with the biomodel-DO index at both
query scale and full-corpus scale, model->AS->GLB-node spatial linkage,
and a materialized three.js viewer pack.
executive.verdict:
The crosswalk loads 2,295 AS rows (1,730 Uberon-keyed, 75.4%) across
116 organ GLBs. A single 25-result query covers only 58/1,730 AS nodes
(liver+pancreas); crossing the full 1,096-model curated corpus covers
635/1,730 (31/114 organs) — an order of magnitude wider, and wide
enough to newly reach kidney. Spatial linkage (10 links/5 models) and
the glomerulus FTU both load correctly, but neither carries live model
results yet: spatial-linkage's readout is a placeholder, and
organ-granularity coverage still overstates fine-grained per-AS-node
evidence. An interactive Atlas Browser (hra-atlas-browser) now presents
all 50 GLB-backed organs with a per-organ model-count gradient and
BioModels links.

decisions_needed.question: Which HRA organs/FTUs have ZERO mechanistic models (the modeling white-space)?
decisions_needed.context: Full-corpus coverage reaches 31/114 organs (27.2%); the other 83 organs, and finer sub-organ FTUs beyond glomerulus, are not yet enumerated as a prioritized gap list.

decisions_needed.question: Does organ-granularity coverage overstate AS-level coverage — can we get finer?
decisions_needed.context: A covered organ's Uberon marks every AS node cut from its GLB as covered, whether or not that specific sub-structure has direct model evidence; 18.3% of crosswalk rows are structurally un-keyable (organizational nodes), a hard ceiling on how fine coverage can ever get.

decisions_needed.question: Can we spatially link model RESULTS (steady-state values) to AS, not just presence?
decisions_needed.context: spatial-linkage's `readout` field is a literal placeholder string ('pending time-series') for all 10 links in v1 — the join topology (model -> AS node) works, but no simulation output is wired to a node yet.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
The full ASCT+B-3D anatomical-structure crosswalk (below the ~81
per-organ reference-organ GLBs) and a sub-organ-scale FTU digital
object are both loadable via thin Steps; crossing the crosswalk with
the hra-integration investigation's biomodel-DO organ->models index is
enough to mark model coverage over anatomical structures and to join
each covered model to the exact GLB scene node it maps to — without a
heavyweight per-AS-node model-matching pipeline.
evidence_for: hra-3d-crosswalk: 2,295 AS rows load, 1,730 (75.4%) Uberon-keyed, across 116 source-organ GLBs — exceeding the ~1,400+ estimate.
model-coverage-3d: the organ-granularity propagation rule fires correctly at query scale (58/1,730 AS nodes, exactly liver+pancreas, nothing else).
corpus-coverage: full-corpus retrieval widens coverage an order of magnitude (635/1,730 AS nodes, 31/114 organs) and newly reaches kidney, which the narrower query misses entirely.
spatial-linkage: the Uberon-only join is deterministic and reproducible (10 links across 5 models, exactly 2 nodes per model, one per sex).
ftu-glomerulus: the sub-organ-scale FTU digital-object shape is real and live-fetchable (confirmed HTTP 200, ~150.4 MB GLB).
caveats: Organ-granularity coverage overstates fine-grained coverage: it marks every AS node cut from a covered organ's GLB, not just nodes with direct model evidence.
Organ-tagging yield is low (82/1,096 = 7.5% of the full corpus), so untagged models may include real anatomical relevance the current synonym matcher misses.
spatial-linkage carries no live model results yet (placeholder readout); the embedded 3D viewer packs render full-corpus coverage, not any single study's own query scope.
Only one FTU (glomerulus) has been exercised; whether the digital-object shape generalizes to other FTUs is unchecked.

studies.name: hra-3d-crosswalk
studies.title: HRA 3D Crosswalk — Full ASCT+B-3D Anatomical-Structure Tree
studies.question:
Does the HRA CDN's ASCT+B-3D models crosswalk load into a Step-driven
composite, giving the full 1,400+ anatomical-structure (AS) tree — not
just the ~81 per-organ reference-organ GLBs — with resolvable Uberon CURIEs
and source-organ GLB names?

resolved_uncertainties: The crosswalk exceeds the original ~1,400+ AS-node estimate (2,295 rows / 1,730 Uberon-keyed), confirming it gives materially finer granularity than the 81 whole-organ GLBs.
remaining_uncertainties: Can the 18.3% organizational/unkeyed rows ever be resolved to Uberon, or is that a permanent ceiling on organ-granularity coverage?

followup_study_proposals.title: Resolve organizational-row Uberon gap
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Attempt to Uberon-key the ~18% organizational/un-keyed crosswalk rows (or confirm the ceiling), improving the AS coverage denominator.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: For each of the 419 `organizational` crosswalk rows, check whether its `parent`/`label` or an adjacent `mesh`/`surface` sibling node resolves to a Uberon CURIE it could inherit, and report how many of the 18.3% un-keyed rows are recoverable vs a genuine structural-grouping ceiling.

findings.statement:
The live ASCT+B-3D crosswalk fetch loads 2,295 anatomical-structure
rows spanning 116 distinct source-organ GLBs; 1,730/2,295 (75.4%)
carry a resolvable UBERON: CURIE, exceeding the ~1,400+ AS-node
original estimate and comfortably clearing the ~81-reference-organ
floor -- confirming the crosswalk gives materially finer anatomical
granularity than the whole-organ GLBs alone.

evidence.summary: 2,295 rows loaded, 116 source-organ GLBs; 1,730/2,295 (75.4%) UBERON-keyed (1,410 mesh + 464 surface rows); 419 organizational rows (18.3%) structurally un-keyable.

biological_validation.basis: The endpoint returns the expected data shape/counts (2,295 rows, exceeding the ~1,400+ estimate) with 75.4% resolvable to Uberon -- the Step-based fetch is accurate to the live crosswalk.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline live fetch and CSV parse of the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk completed without error.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 quantifies the 75.4% Uberon-density ceiling that bounds every downstream organ-granularity coverage computation (model-coverage-3d, corpus-coverage).

derived.insight:
The live ASCT+B-3D crosswalk fetch loads 2,295 anatomical-structure
rows spanning 116 distinct source-organ GLBs; 1,730/2,295 (75.4%)
carry a resolvable UBERON: CURIE, exceeding the ~1,400+ AS-node
original estimate and comfortably clearing the ~81-reference-organ
floor -- confirming the crosswalk gives materially finer anatomical
granularity than the whole-organ GLBs alone.

studies.name: model-coverage-3d
studies.title: Model Coverage 3D — AS/Organ Coverage from BioModel-DO Annotations
studies.question:
Of the HRA ASCT+B-3D crosswalk's 1,400+ anatomical structures (and ~81
reference organs), which are covered by a mechanistic model — and can
that coverage be viewed directly on the 3D anatomy?

resolved_uncertainties: The organ-granularity propagation rule is verified correct at this scope: coverage is exactly as broad as the underlying organ annotation (liver+pancreas), not artificially inflated.
remaining_uncertainties: Does full-corpus retrieval reach organs this query misses (kidney)? See corpus-coverage.
Does organ-granularity propagation overstate coverage for fine AS nodes with no direct model evidence?

followup_study_proposals.title: AS-level (sub-organ) model coverage
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Annotate models to specific anatomical structures (not just whole organs) so coverage reflects direct per-AS evidence rather than organ-granularity propagation.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Parse SBML MIRIAM/Uberon annotations at the anatomical-structure level (not just organ-name synonym matching) for the biomodel-DO catalog, cross the result directly against crosswalk AS nodes, and compare AS-level covered counts against the current organ-granularity-propagated coverage to quantify the overstatement.

findings.statement:
Crossing the 25-result "glucose regulation" biomodel-DO catalog
against the 1,730-Uberon-row crosswalk marks 58/1,730 AS nodes
covered (3.4%), all propagating from exactly the 4 source-organ GLBs
whose Uberon is organ-tagged by the underlying catalog (liver +
pancreas, both sexes) -- confirming the organ-granularity propagation
rule fires correctly rather than overstating coverage at this scope.

evidence.summary: 58/1,730 AS nodes covered (3.4%), 4/114 organ GLBs (VH_F_Liver, VH_M_Liver, VH_F_Pancreas, VH_M_Pancreas); no kidney coverage at this query scope.

biological_validation.basis: Coverage is organ-granularity, name-based propagation from a 25-result query, not calibrated per-AS-node model evidence -- real (liver+pancreas light up exactly where the underlying catalog is organ-tagged, nothing else does) but recall-limited to this query's scope, so gated needs_calibration rather than passed.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline coverage-crossing composite (25-result query x crosswalk) completed without error.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 confirms the propagation rule is correct at this scope, but organ-granularity still overstates fine-grained coverage (a covered organ's Uberon marks every AS node cut from its GLB, not just nodes with direct model evidence) -- the study's central caveat.

derived.insight:
Crossing the 25-result "glucose regulation" biomodel-DO catalog
against the 1,730-Uberon-row crosswalk marks 58/1,730 AS nodes
covered (3.4%), all propagating from exactly the 4 source-organ GLBs
whose Uberon is organ-tagged by the underlying catalog (liver +
pancreas, both sexes) -- confirming the organ-granularity propagation
rule fires correctly rather than overstating coverage at this scope.

studies.name: spatial-linkage
studies.title: Spatial Linkage — Model -> AS -> GLB Scene-Node Links
studies.question:
For each biomodel-DO organ annotation, exactly which ASCT+B-3D crosswalk
GLB scene node(s) does it correspond to — precise enough for a 3D viewer
to color/label the right node per model?

resolved_uncertainties: Uberon-only join reliably produces exactly 2 links per model (one per sex), confirming the join mechanism is deterministic and reproducible.
remaining_uncertainties: Can we spatially link model RESULTS (steady-state values), not just organ presence, to a specific AS node?
Is Uberon-CURIE-only join precise enough, or does a real viewer need a single 'best' node resolved per model?

followup_study_proposals.title: Result-driven spatial linkage
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Color AS nodes by a real model readout (steady-state concentration from the corpus dataset) instead of a placeholder string, so the 3D viewer shows results, not just coverage.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Extract steady-state species concentrations from the committed corpus COPASI/Tellurium comparison dataset and attach them as the `readout` field on each (model, AS-node) link, replacing the placeholder 'pending time-series' string; re-render the 3D viewer pack colored by that value.

findings.statement:
The live Uberon-only join produces 10 (model, GLB-node) links across
5 distinct biomodels, with every model linking to exactly 2 nodes
(one per sex) -- confirming the join mechanism is deterministic and
reproducible from the shared organ Uberon, even though `readout` is
still a literal placeholder string ("pending time-series") for every
link in v1.

evidence.summary: 10 links across 5 models (BIOMD0000000633 -> liver x2; MODEL2001080002, MODEL1112110004, BIOMD0000000382, BIOMD0000000372 -> pancreas x2 each); 2 links per model, one per sex.

biological_validation.basis: The join topology is verified correct (every model links to exactly 2 sex-split nodes), but `readout` is a placeholder string for every link -- no simulation result is actually linked to a node yet, so this is gated needs_calibration rather than passed.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline spatial-link join composite (biomodel-DO organs x crosswalk rows on shared Uberon) completed without error.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 establishes the join mechanism works reliably (10 links/5 models, Uberon-only, fully reproducible) but carries no result data yet -- model->AS->node linkage works at the topology level only.

derived.insight:
The live Uberon-only join produces 10 (model, GLB-node) links across
5 distinct biomodels, with every model linking to exactly 2 nodes
(one per sex) -- confirming the join mechanism is deterministic and
reproducible from the shared organ Uberon, even though `readout` is
still a literal placeholder string ("pending time-series") for every
link in v1.

studies.name: ftu-glomerulus
studies.title: FTU Glomerulus — 3D Functional-Tissue-Unit Digital Object
studies.question:
Does the HRA CDN's glomerulus 3D functional-tissue-unit (FTU) digital
object load into a Step-driven composite, giving a sub-organ-scale 3D
asset (below the per-organ reference-organ GLBs) that could anchor
finer-grained model coverage?

resolved_uncertainties: The glomerulus FTU digital object is live, correctly shaped, and resolves to a real GLB asset (after the Accept-header fix).
remaining_uncertainties: Are enough FTUs beyond glomerulus published at this same digital-object shape to generalize sub-organ-scale model coverage?

followup_study_proposals.title: FTU-scale model coverage
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Extend model coverage from whole-organ GLBs down to functional tissue units (glomerulus + other published FTUs) so sub-organ models can be anchored.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Fetch every published HRA FTU digital object (not just glomerulus), cross their sub-organ anatomical structures against the biomodel-DO organ->models index, and report coverage at FTU granularity alongside the existing organ-granularity figures.

findings.statement:
The glomerulus 3D FTU digital object loads live: title "glomerulus
(v1.0) graph data", version v1.0 (HuBMAP, CC BY 4.0), resolving to a
real, confirmed-live (HTTP 200) glb_url of ~150.4 MB -- confirming the
sub-organ-scale FTU digital-object shape is real and fetchable, a
prerequisite for anchoring finer-than-whole-organ model coverage.

evidence.summary: ftu record loads with non-empty title/description/version; glb_url resolves HTTP 200 at ~150.4 MB (~143.4 MiB); required an Accept:application/json header fix to the client for the live CCF resolver to 200 rather than 404.

biological_validation.basis: The endpoint returns the expected digital-object shape/data -- title, description, version, and a resolving GLB asset confirmed live (HTTP 200, ~150.4 MB).

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline live fetch of the glomerulus FTU digital object completed without error (after the Accept-header fix).

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 establishes the sub-organ-scale FTU digital-object shape is real and fetchable, directly bearing on whether sub-organ-scale model coverage can generalize beyond whole-organ granularity.

derived.insight:
The glomerulus 3D FTU digital object loads live: title "glomerulus
(v1.0) graph data", version v1.0 (HuBMAP, CC BY 4.0), resolving to a
real, confirmed-live (HTTP 200) glb_url of ~150.4 MB -- confirming the
sub-organ-scale FTU digital-object shape is real and fetchable, a
prerequisite for anchoring finer-than-whole-organ model coverage.

studies.name: corpus-coverage
studies.title: Corpus Coverage — Full 1,096-Model BioModels Catalog on HRA 3D Anatomy
studies.question:
Of the HRA ASCT+B-3D crosswalk's 1,730 Uberon-keyed anatomical structures
(across 114 source-organ GLBs), how many are covered once every curated
BioModels model — not just a narrow search query — is crossed against
them, and does full-corpus coverage reach organs a single-query search
misses (e.g. kidney)?

resolved_uncertainties: Full-corpus retrieval materially widens coverage over a single query (635 vs 58 AS nodes) and newly reaches kidney, confirming retrieval breadth is a real, measurable lever independent of query choice.
remaining_uncertainties: Does the low 7.5% organ-tagging yield undercount real anatomical relevance among the untagged 1,014 models?
Which HRA organs/FTUs have zero mechanistic-model coverage even at full-corpus scale (the modeling white-space)?

followup_study_proposals.title: Coverage gap analysis
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Enumerate HRA organs/FTUs with zero mechanistic-model coverage even at full-corpus scale, to prioritize where new modeling work would have the most impact.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Cross the full corpus-coverage organ->models index against the complete 114-organ-GLB / 1,730-AS-node crosswalk to list every organ/AS-node with zero covering models, ranked by AS-node count, as a prioritized modeling-gap report.

findings.statement:
Crossing the full 1,096-model curated BioModels catalog (82/1,096,
7.5%, organ-tagged) against the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk covers 635 AS
nodes (36.7%) across 31 distinct organ GLBs (27.2%) -- an order of
magnitude wider than the 25-result glucose-regulation query's 58 AS
nodes / 4 organs, and critically newly reaches kidney, confirming
full-corpus retrieval finds anatomically relevant models a single
search term misses entirely.

evidence.summary: 635/1,730 AS nodes covered (36.7%), 31/114 organ GLBs (27.2%), including kidney (VH_F_Kidney_L/_R, VH_M_Kidney_L/_R); catalog 1,096/1,096 retrieved, 82 (7.5%) organ-tagged; vs 58/1,730 AS nodes / 4 organs for the 25-result query (model-coverage-3d).

biological_validation.basis: Coverage is organ-granularity, name-based tagging (82/1,096 = 7.5% of the corpus tagged), not calibrated per-AS-node model evidence -- real and an order of magnitude wider than the query-scoped study (635 vs 58 AS nodes), but recall-limited by the current synonym-matching tagger, so gated needs_calibration rather than passed.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline full-corpus coverage-crossing composite (committed catalog x crosswalk) completed without error.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 shows full-corpus retrieval, not just query choice, is the coverage bottleneck -- it finds anatomically relevant models a single search term misses entirely (kidney newly covered) -- the study's central interpretive claim.

derived.insight:
Crossing the full 1,096-model curated BioModels catalog (82/1,096,
7.5%, organ-tagged) against the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk covers 635 AS
nodes (36.7%) across 31 distinct organ GLBs (27.2%) -- an order of
magnitude wider than the 25-result glucose-regulation query's 58 AS
nodes / 4 organs, and critically newly reaches kidney, confirming
full-corpus retrieval finds anatomically relevant models a single
search term misses entirely.

studies.name: ftu-model-coverage
studies.title: FTU Model Coverage — Do Existing BioModels Model HRA Functional Tissue Units?
studies.question:
Do existing BioModels model HRA functional tissue units (FTUs) -- Katy
Boerner's question -- and, for the FTUs that already have models, can HRA
CTpop (Cell Type Populations) cell-type counts parameterize them, per the
RUI -> CTpop -> model vision Peter Hunter and SPARC-heart describe?

resolved_uncertainties: Existing BioModels do already model several HRA FTUs at real, named-model granularity -- pancreatic islet (3), colon crypt (4), cardiac muscle/myocardium (3), liver lobule (2), skin epidermis (1) -- directly answering Katy Boerner's question in the affirmative for these five.

The islet's characteristic cell types (beta/alpha/delta, CL:0000169/0171/0173) are identifiable as candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs for the covered islet models, confirming the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization seam is at least well-defined for a covered FTU.
remaining_uncertainties: Six FTUs (kidney glomerulus, kidney nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine crypt-villus axis, ovarian follicle, lymph node follicle) have zero matching models at this granularity -- is that a real modeling gap, or a name-matching recall failure?

Does binding a REAL HRA CTpop cell-type count (not just identifying candidate cell types) to the Topp2000/Jiang2007/Bertram2007 islet models' beta-cell-mass parameters materially change their calibration?

followup_study_proposals.title: Bind HRA CTpop islet cell counts to the islet-model parameters
followup_study_proposals.motivation: ctpop_parameter_stub identifies the islet's beta/alpha/delta cell types as candidate CTpop-parameterizable inputs but binds no real count; a real RUI-registered islet's measured cell-type proportions would let the Topp2000/Jiang2007/Bertram2007 islet models be re-parameterized against actual measured tissue composition rather than literature-default beta-cell-mass values.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Fetch a real HRA CTpop result for a RUI-registered pancreatic-islet tissue block (per-anatomical-structure beta/alpha/delta-cell counts/proportions), map those counts onto the Topp2000/Jiang2007/Bertram2007 islet models' beta-cell-mass (or equivalent cell-population) parameters, and compare simulated output against the models' literature-default parameterization.

findings.statement:
Crossing the full 1,096-model curated BioModels corpus against a
curated 11-FTU list by name/synonym substring match covers 5/11 FTUs
(45.5%), matching 13 distinct models: pancreatic islet of Langerhans
(3 models), colon crypt of Lieberkuhn (4 models, all Smallbone2013
Colon Crypt cycle versions), cardiac muscle/myocardium unit (3
models, SPARC-heart-relevant), liver lobule (2 models), and skin
epidermis unit (1 model). Six FTUs (kidney glomerulus, kidney
nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine crypt-villus axis, ovarian
follicle, lymph node follicle) match zero models -- existing
BioModels do already model several HRA FTUs, but real modeling
white-space remains for the rest.

evidence.summary: 5/11 FTUs covered (45.5%), 13 distinct models matched: islet=3 (Jiang2007, Bertram2007, Wierschem2004), colon crypt=4 (Smallbone2013 v0-v3), cardiac muscle=3 (Cooling2007, McDougal2017, Zhou2024), liver lobule=2, skin epidermis=1; 0 for glomerulus/nephron/alveolus/villus/ovarian follicle/lymph node follicle.

biological_validation.basis: Coverage is name/synonym substring matching (not curated per-model FTU annotation or model-content inspection) and the CTpop parameterization seam is a v1 stub with no real cell-type count bound to any model parameter yet, so gated needs_calibration rather than passed -- but the underlying model hits (islet, colon crypt, cardiac muscle, liver lobule, skin epidermis) are real, named, resolvable BioModels IDs.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline ftu-model-coverage composite (committed catalog x curated HRA_FTUS list) completed without error, emitting a non-empty ftu_coverage list and summary.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 directly answers Katy Boerner's question -- yes, existing BioModels do model several HRA FTUs already (5/11, 13 models) -- while also enumerating the six FTUs with zero current coverage, the study's central interpretive claim.

derived.insight:
Crossing the full 1,096-model curated BioModels corpus against a
curated 11-FTU list by name/synonym substring match covers 5/11 FTUs
(45.5%), matching 13 distinct models: pancreatic islet of Langerhans
(3 models), colon crypt of Lieberkuhn (4 models, all Smallbone2013
Colon Crypt cycle versions), cardiac muscle/myocardium unit (3
models, SPARC-heart-relevant), liver lobule (2 models), and skin
epidermis unit (1 model). Six FTUs (kidney glomerulus, kidney
nephron, lung alveolus, small-intestine crypt-villus axis, ovarian
follicle, lymph node follicle) match zero models -- existing
BioModels do already model several HRA FTUs, but real modeling
white-space remains for the rest.

studies.name: ctpop-islet-parameterization
studies.title: CTpop -> Topp2000 Islet Parameterization — Beta-Cell Composition Shifts the Glucose Setpoint
studies.question:
Does binding HRA CTpop islet cell-type composition to the Topp2000
beta-cell-mass model (BIOMD0000000341) change the predicted glucose
regulation -- realizing the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization vision
Katy Boerner / Peter Hunter / SPARC describe, for the pancreatic islet FTU
`ftu-model-coverage` already found covered?

resolved_uncertainties: CTpop islet composition, bound as an initial-condition parameter (beta-cell mass), does mechanistically change Topp2000's predicted glucose regulation -- realizing (for one covered FTU model and one composition-to-parameter binding) the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization vision `ftu-model-coverage`'s `ctpop_parameter_stub` only stubbed.

The composition shift from healthy (54% beta) to T2D-relevant beta-depleted (30% beta) composition is large enough, in this model's parameterization, to cross a real bifurcation between the model's physiological and pathological fixed points -- not just perturb a number within one regime.
remaining_uncertainties: Does a LIVE HRA CTpop count (for a specific RUI-registered islet tissue block) differ materially from the documented literature-average composition used here, and if so, in which direction?

Should alpha/delta cell fractions bind to separate Topp2000-family or extended-model parameters (e.g. a glucagon-secretion term), rather than folding all islet composition information into the single beta-cell-mass initial condition?

followup_study_proposals.title: Bind a LIVE HRA CTpop islet cell count (not documented literature values) to Topp2000
followup_study_proposals.motivation: This study proves the mechanism (composition -> beta-cell mass -> glucose regime) using documented literature composition; a live per-tissue-block CTpop count would let a specific RUI-registered islet be parameterized against its own measured composition rather than a population average.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: When/if a live HRA CTpop JSON endpoint becomes available for a RUI-registered pancreatic-islet tissue block, fetch its real beta/alpha/delta-cell counts, compute the beta fraction from the real counts (not the documented 0.54/0.34/0.10/0.02 split), and re-run `compare_islet_compositions` with that live fraction in place of the documented one.

followup_study_proposals.title: Bind alpha/delta CTpop fractions to per-cell-type Topp-family model parameters
followup_study_proposals.motivation: This study binds only the beta fraction (to initial beta-cell mass); a fuller CTpop -> model parameterization would also bind alpha/delta fractions to whichever islet-model parameters they mechanistically govern (e.g. a glucagon-secretion-capable extended model).
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Identify or build an islet model with explicit alpha/delta-cell-mediated terms (e.g. glucagon counter-regulation), and bind CTpop alpha/delta fractions to those terms alongside the existing beta -> B binding, then compare against the beta-only binding used here.

findings.statement:
Binding the documented healthy islet composition (54% beta) to
Topp2000's initial beta-cell mass reproduces the model's own default
(b_ref=37) and the model settles at its physiological fixed point
(glucose ~100 mg/dL over 4,000 model-days). Binding the documented
T2D-relevant beta-depleted composition (30% beta) scales the initial
mass down to ~20.56 and the identical model crosses Topp2000's
beta-cell-mass bifurcation into its pathological fixed point (glucose
~600 mg/dL, beta-cell mass and insulin collapsing toward 0) -- the
CTpop composition mechanistically shifts which of the model's two
stable regimes the glucose trajectory lands in, not merely its
numeric value.

evidence.summary: healthy (beta=0.54, b_init=37=b_ref): G 250->100.0, B 37->300.0, I 2.8->10.0 (physiological fixed point). beta_depleted (beta=0.30, b_init=20.56): G 250->600.0, B 20.56->~0, I 2.8->~0 (pathological fixed point) -- same model, same 4,000-model-day horizon, differing only in the CTpop-composition-bound initial beta-cell mass.

biological_validation.basis: ISLET_COMPOSITION is documented literature/HRA-ASCT+B composition (Cabrera 2006 PNAS; Brissova 2005), not a live HRA CTpop API pull, and the binding is initial-mass-only (alpha/delta fractions identified but not bound to a model parameter), so gated needs_calibration rather than passed -- but the underlying model (BIOMD0000000341) is real and the binding (B_init = b_ref * beta_fraction / 0.54, b_ref read from the SBML) is a defensible, documented, non-hardcoded parameterization.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline ctpop-islet-parameterization composite (CtpopIsletParameterizationStep -> compare_islet_compositions) completed without error for both scenarios, emitting non-empty runs.healthy / runs.beta_depleted trajectories with real BioModels-fetched, tellurium-solved numbers.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 directly answers the study question -- yes, binding CTpop islet composition to Topp2000 changes the predicted glucose regulation, and dramatically: it flips which of the model's two stable fixed points (physiological vs. pathological/diabetic) the trajectory settles into, realizing the RUI -> CTpop -> model parameterization vision for a real, covered FTU model rather than merely stubbing which parameters would be involved.

studies.name: blood-vasculature-network
studies.title: Blood Vasculature Network — VCCF transport graph to couple organ models
studies.question:
Can the HRA/VCCF vasculature data define a whole-body blood-transport
network — a directed heart -> organ -> heart circuit through named vessels —
that we can use to COUPLE independent organ simulations by advecting shared
blood-borne solutes (glucose, O2, insulin, ...) between them? And what does a
v1 blood-circulation simulation over that network look like?
studies.discovery_implications:
Establishes the blood-transport network as the connective substrate that lets
this atlas's organ models stop being islands: with per-edge flow and a shared
plasma compartment, a change in one organ's solute exchange propagates to the
others with a physiologically-ordered transport delay. Next: implement the
BloodTransportProcess and couple the glucose-regulation organ models as the
first circulating multi-organ composite.

findings.statement:
The VCCF data yields a fully closed whole-body transport graph: all 28
FTU routes start and end at a heart chamber (28 closed circuits, 0 open),
spanning 191 vessels and 444 directed flow edges (94 artery / 20
capillary / 73 vein / 4 chamber). The topology substrate for coupling
organ models is therefore complete and validated.

A blood-circulation simulation is designed on this graph (see
docs/blood-circulation-simulation-plan.md): a BloodTransportProcess
advects a shared plasma solute vector along the edges at flow rates Q set
by a hemodynamic model (resistance network or the Font-Clos 2020
cardiac-output partition), and each organ node is an existing organ
Process exchanging solutes with the blood perfusing it. Glucose
regulation (liver <-> pancreas <-> muscle) is the proposed first coupling.
findings.evidence: Design doc + the Font-Clos et al. 2020 whole-body organ-flow-network precedent (references/papers.bib).

studies.name: hra-atlas-browser
studies.title: HRA Atlas Browser — organ selector + model-count gradient + BioModels links
studies.question:
Can we present the full HRA-3D model-coverage picture as an interactive
atlas: pick any of the 50 GLB-backed HRA organs, see its regions
demarcated and colored by how many mechanistic models are associated with
it, and browse straight to those BioModels?

resolved_uncertainties: The full 50-organ GLB set is enumerable and renderable with a per-organ model-count gradient and BioModels links.
remaining_uncertainties: Can sub-region (AS-level) counts replace organ-granularity coloring? See fp-as-level-coverage.

followup_study_proposals.title: AS-level (sub-organ) model coverage in the Atlas Browser
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Color sub-regions within an organ by their own model count instead of inheriting the organ's count.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Parse SBML MIRIAM/Uberon annotations at anatomical-structure granularity, join to crosswalk AS nodes, and drive per-mesh color from per-node counts.

findings.statement:
The atlas manifest enumerates all 50 GLB-backed HRA organs and colors
the 14 modeled ones by model count (blood 51 max, 167 distinct models),
linking each to its BioModels entries — a whole-atlas overview of where
mechanistic modeling exists.
